pr_title: ao_coreaudio: use device's nominal sample rate for latency properties
pr_body: Fixes sync issues when using high-latency devices at non-native sample rates. Closes #10984.
pr_comments:
For reference, this mailing list post is one of the few places that explicitly notes of this being the case https://lists.apple.com/archives/coreaudio-api/2010/Jan/msg00046.html .

> - All the HAL properties I mentioned above are counting in sample frames at the Device's nominal sample rate.

And once you realize that, it is quite obvious as it's where the properties are being queried from :)
Merged as 2fa1e7d0b409f2ceb608d9b6c5d90106507595aa (since the file seems to adhere to ~80 columns I moved the last argument of `CA_GET_O` to its own line).

issue_context.title: Bad A/V sync with bluetooth headphones on some files
issue_context.body:
### Important Information

- mpv 25b66256d7ff48254b2055a066e29f260414112f
- macOS 13.0.1 (22A400)
- Local build

### Reproduction steps

- Connect Bluetooth headphones (I'm using AirPods Max to test)
- Play back the attached file

### Expected behavior

Audio is in sync with video

### Actual behavior

Audio is roughly 100ms ahead of video

### Log file

https://gist.github.com/04df40c1d27f72b5310bad8478a4f82f

### Sample files

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/819638/206798833-d74255fc-52ef-4b46-9f64-2093395af3a6.mp4

review_comments: Is it worth doing this once during setup and storing the value? Or do you expect it can change?
Hm never mind I think this already only happens once. Misunderstood the context.

Yup. In theory we might have to update the values during runtime with listening for changes or so when the device configuration changes, but I don't think that is currently being handled really at this moment, either.

So as such this is explicitly an improvement :) .
